Definition: to stretch a bow, as an archer
BiblicalUsage: Hagar goes and sits down over against Ishmael a good way off, as it were a bowshot, and says, let me not see the death of the child. The word is the bowshot itself, the distance of an archer's shot. It appears once, measuring how far a mother can bear to sit from her dying son.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the bowshot is one of the Bible's most human measures: far enough not to watch, close enough to hear, and God hears the boy's voice from exactly there.
